correctness.rationale: The independent simplex enumeration gives exactly 244 nonempty faces, partitioned into chord stars and sixteen exceptional triangles. Nerve identification reduces the integral second homology to a 20-by-16 signed triangle boundary kernel. The rank-13 unit-determinant minor, three explicit exact cycles and identity-coordinate rows prove a saturated rank-three integral basis. Permuting oriented triples gives integer R and S matrices. A four-cycle with a primitive 3-by-3 determinant-one submatrix generates the entire lattice and obeys the reflection relation, determining the claimed integral dihedral module. Gcd of Smith minors of R-I is (1,1,4), and modulo two the powers have ranks 2,1,0. Direct full-face signed Lefschetz tests of 16 group elements agree. Braun supplies the previously known homology concentration. All statements follow by finite proof, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: This is the first nontrivial rank-three representation case in the natural stable two-subset Kneser sphere-wedge family, not an arbitrary chosen subcomplex. The exact integral D8 action and cyclic order-four coinvariants distinguish a nonsplit lattice from the rationally identical split sign-plus-quarter-turn module. Such an extension obstruction is invisible to both the established Betti rank and the published full rational character, providing a meaningful structural refinement and a reproducible test case for integral equivariant topology.
